sentences.latin: Agricola agrum magnum habet.
sentences.english: The farmer has a large field.

sentences.latin: Filius agricolae equum album habet.
sentences.english: The farmer's son has a white horse.

sentences.latin: Mater cibum bonum parat.
sentences.english: The mother prepares good food.

sentences.latin: Filius aquam multam portat.
sentences.english: The son carries much water.

sentences.latin: Ager a cane fideli custoditur.
sentences.english: The field is guarded by the loyal dog.

sentences.latin: Nam agricola canem nigrum amat.
sentences.english: For the farmer loves the black dog.

sentences.latin: Equus filium ad silvam portat.
sentences.english: The horse carries the son to the forest.

sentences.latin: Filius flores pulchros capit.
sentences.english: The son takes beautiful flowers.

sentences.latin: Filius avem albam videt.
sentences.english: The son sees a white bird.

sentences.latin: Sed avis equum terret.
sentences.english: But the bird frightens the horse.

sentences.latin: Filius equum fortem servat.
sentences.english: The son protects the strong horse.

sentences.latin: Equus filium ad agrum portat.
sentences.english: The horse carries the son to the field.

sentences.latin: Filius matri flores dat.
sentences.english: The son gives the flowers to the mother.

sentences.latin: Filius bonus a matre laudatur.
sentences.english: The good son is praised by the mother.

sentences.latin: Itaque familia cibum et vinum habet.
sentences.english: And so the family has food and wine.

sentences.latin: Rex iustus poetam clarum ad urbem magnam vocat.
sentences.english: The just king calls the famous poet to the great city.

sentences.latin: Poeta librum pulchrum ad regem portat.
sentences.english: The poet carries a beautiful book to the king.

sentences.latin: Rex verba poetae audit et librum laudat.
sentences.english: The king hears the poet's words and praises the book.

sentences.latin: Liber pulcher in urbe nostra laudatur.
sentences.english: The beautiful book is praised in our city.

sentences.latin: Rex filio suo librum poetae dat.
sentences.english: The king gives the poet's book to his own son.

sentences.latin: Filius regis librum aperit et verba clara videt.
sentences.english: The king's son opens the book and sees the clear words.

sentences.latin: Itaque filius regis poetam laudat et donum parat.
sentences.english: And so the king's son praises the poet and prepares a gift.

sentences.latin: Sed magister miser gloriae poetae invidet.
sentences.english: But a wretched teacher envies the poet's glory.

sentences.latin: Is magister contra poetam verba gravia dicit.
sentences.english: That teacher speaks severe words against the poet.

sentences.latin: Sed rex iustus poetam fidelem servat.
sentences.english: But the just king protects the loyal poet.

sentences.latin: Magister miser ex urbe magna mittitur.
sentences.english: The wretched teacher is sent out of the great city.

sentences.latin: Poeta librum novum de rege scribit.
sentences.english: The poet writes a new book about the king.

sentences.latin: Nam populus urbis verba dulcia poetae amat.
sentences.english: For the people of the city love the poet's sweet words.

sentences.latin: Itaque donum magnum viro claro datur.
sentences.english: And so a great gift is given to the famous man.

sentences.latin: Poeta librum novum regi iusto dat.
sentences.english: The poet gives the new book to the just king.

sentences.latin: Dux fortis legionis nostrae vallum altum et longum munit.
sentences.english: The brave leader of our legion fortifies the high and long rampart.

sentences.latin: Vexillum rubrum ducis sapientis a militibus fidelibus tollitur.
sentences.english: The red banner of the wise leader is raised by the loyal soldiers.

sentences.latin: Sed cohors nostra ab hostibus ferocibus sagittis multis petitur.
sentences.english: But our cohort is attacked by the fierce enemies with many arrows.

sentences.latin: Milites fortes cohortis nostrae hostes feroces hastis longis terrent.
sentences.english: The brave soldiers of our cohort frighten the fierce enemies with long spears.

sentences.latin: Itaque milites nostri victoriam magnam et pacem longam habent.
sentences.english: And so our soldiers have a great victory and a long peace.
